thread:
maria: heads-up, encountered a goroutine leak in the go sdk generator sample when cancelling the parent ctx mid-stream. app exits but background goroutine keeps pulling from the stream and never returns.

maria: repro steps: start generator stream, cancel ctx after ~10s. process exits but `ps` shows a goroutine stuck on network read. observed on sdk v0.8.0.

maria: minimal repro snippet:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
c := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
stream, _ := c.GeneratorStream(ctx, req)
go func() {
    for ch := range stream.Chunks() {
        fmt.Print(ch.Text)
    }
}()
// simulate user cancel after 10s
time.Sleep(10 * time.Second)
cancel()
// main returns, but background goroutine remains blocked
```

maria: logs show `read tcp ...: connection reset by peer` then nothing. no final error is surfaced.

tian: thanks, this sounds related to how we tear down the transport on ctx cancel. the generator stream goroutine might be `range`ing on a channel that's only closed by the network reader when it exits normally, but if ctx cancels we bail out earlier and don't close the consumer channel.

kevin: two quick asks: (1) can you confirm if calling `stream.Close()` before cancel fixes it? (2) are you using `Wait()`/`Err()` pattern? we recently added `Wait()` in the beta, maybe sample app didn't pick it up.

maria: tried `stream.Close()` and that helps if you call it, but onboarding sample doesn't. a new user likely won't call Close() because they expect context to be sufficient. `Wait()` isn't present in v0.8.0 for our app, so no.

alla: this is an ergonomics problem. ctx cancel should deterministically close the stream and cause the `Chunks()` range to end with a clear error (context.Canceled). otherwise sample apps are fragile.

runtime-bot: deploy-note: runtime-transport 1.12.0 rolled at 2026-03-01T09:00:00Z (recent change: aggressive reconnect backoff).

kevin: implementation idea: on GeneratorStream we spawn a monitor goroutine that watches ctx.Done() and if closed, call stream.internalCloseWithError(ctx.Err()). That will unblock the consumer channel with a sentinel error. Also expose `Stream.Err() error` to read final error.

tian: agree. we should also audit the reconnect path: if a reconnect attempt happens at the same time as ctx cancel, we may race and leave the consumer in limbo. test matrix: normal finish, ctx cancel before any msgs, ctx cancel during reconnect, token refresh mid-stream + ctx cancel.

maria: QA note: i saw a variant where token refresh + ctx cancel resulted in main goroutine returning but test harness flagged leaked goroutines. repro for QA attached to the issue.

kevin: let's do a small API ergonomics change in the next patch: ensure ctx cancellation always closes Chunks() and make `Err()` return context.Canceled if appropriate. keep the existing streaming semantics otherwise. add a tiny sample in generator-stream-demo that shows `defer stream.Close()` and `if err := stream.Wait(); err != nil { log.Println(err) }`.

alla: also propose we update docs/quickstart: "Contexts control request lifetime, but callers should still `defer stream.Close()` or call `stream.Wait()` to observe final error." that helps with onboarding friction.

runtime-bot: issue-created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/issues/430 - "go: generator stream should close on ctx cancel and surface Err()"

qa-bot: test-plan: add e2e that cancels ctx during long stream, assert no goroutine leaks, assert `Err()` == context.Canceled or wrapped error.

maria: thanks all. i'll pick up QA validation after the patch lands. assigning: tian will own SDK fix, kevin will update sample app and quickstart, alla will update docs. will re-run harness once merged. :thumbsup:
